BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's Update Draft and Disclosure Letter

## Threshold point: "FINAL / agreed / market standard"

The cover note and preamble say the positions were "settled at principal level", are "FINAL", and reflect "market standard" terms. None of that is verified, and our process doesn't accept it on the Seller's say-so. I have no record of any such agreement. Please confirm with Amelia Frost whether she agreed anything with the Seller's principal. Unless she did, treat every position below as an open Seller proposal. The "market" ranges are the Seller's own assertions with no support.

**Watch the 20% cap and 18-month period.** Both match our fallbacks, but a number matching a fallback does not clear it. Each fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given. We should not signal acceptance, even informally.

## Where the Seller departs from the playbook

| Item | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start | Unauthorised fallback. Counter at 25%. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. Reject. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, **excess only** | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** | Both the size and the mechanism are wrong. Reject. |
| Claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months | Unauthorised fallback. Counter at 24. |
| Limitation override (12.3/13) | Limits apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise | Separate regimes, no hidden override | Reject. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same cap and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime, 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Reject. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims "of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything | Reject. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable | Delete | Reject. |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours, satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent and evidence its conditions are met before Completion | Reject. |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Post-Completion release | Payout, direct repayment, effective releases at Completion | Reject. |
| DD-005 bonuses | Not in funds flow | Line item or seller-funded, with on-costs | Reject. |
| Ironquay (11.1) | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment | Broaden, preserve the SOW3 cure | Reject. |
| DD-006 incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve, investigate, update | Reframe. |
| Sandbar | "Ordinary-course" | Assess, no automatic Debt | Hold. |
| Tax/IP | "Settled under general regime" | Open | Reject. |
| Title | DD-012 register | Independent evidence | Reject as sufficient. |

## Reasoning on the material issues

### 1. Liability architecture (the most serious problem)
The Seller's drafting, read together, collapses everything into one regime.
- **Fundamental and fraud claims would be capped and time-barred.** Applying the general cap to Title and capacity warranties would cap our recovery for not owning 100% of the shares at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m price. Applying the 18-month period would extinguish that claim well before any realistic discovery date.
- **Fraud would be limited.** The "all Claims of any nature" language in 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 would, on its face, cover fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. Nobody on our side may waive that carve-out. Insert an express override to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **The limitation clause overrides the specific regimes.** The sentence in 12.3/13 that limits apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a hidden general-regime override. Reverse it. Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment and covenant claims should each have their own stated limits, and the general limits should apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- **The basket is a deductible.** The Seller's "excess only" basket means we absorb the first AUD 250,000 on top of the 25,000 per-claim floor. That is materially worse than our AUD 50,000 tipping basket, even if the numbers were closer.

### 2. Disclosure and knowledge
Whole-data-room disclosure plus public registers, combined with clause 8.3, would let the Seller disclose against every warranty simply by populating the data room. Clause 8.3 also bars claims for anything "discoverable", which is effectively a prudent-search standard. The defence would reach title, capacity and specific indemnities as well. We should:
- strike 8.3;
- limit disclosure to specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties;
- offer, at most, a seller-knowledge qualifier with named knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, which can never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

Disclosure Letter para 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable only if it doesn't dilute specific indemnities or the fair-disclosure standard.

### 3. Conditions and Completion deliverables
The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its SPA drafting.

- **Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).** DL para 2 admits there is no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. The SPA nonetheless offers only reasonable endeavours, with consent "satisfied on delivery". Make it a condition precedent that the Bluefen consent is effective, unconditional or with its conditions evidenced as met, and in a form we approve. Reasonable endeavours is not enough for a material customer. We should also decide whether the CP is waivable by us alone.
- **Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m).** DL para 3 confirms the facility isn't repaid and no discharge is in the data room. Require a current payout letter, repayment direct from Completion funds, and security releases effective on payment. A post-Completion release is a fallback only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists. The price mechanics must also stay debt-free/cash-free.
- **Bonuses (AUD 420,000).** The Seller says this is "a matter for the Seller" but leaves it out of the funds flow. We want either a specific line item or an express seller-funded obligation. DL para 5 doesn't say whether payroll tax, super or other on-costs apply, so require the Seller to confirm and bear any triggered on-costs. The funds flow shouldn't silently exclude them.

### 4. Matters to handle without assuming outcomes
- **Ironquay (AUD 180,000).** DL para 4 says DD-010's figure isn't independent bank verification, and no receipt or assignment is in the data room. We should not assume it's owed or paid. Ask for payment evidence and a confirmatory SOW3 assignment, keep the SOW3 cure mechanism, and broaden the indemnity beyond "the SOW3 payment" to cover third-party IP claims, ownership of the Project Materials and associated costs. The Seller calling it "adequate" is not a reason to leave it narrow.
- **DD-006 incident.** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is unsupported. Its own letter says it can't establish access, scope or notification duty. Equally, we should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any dollar figure. Ask for log preservation, a documented investigation, regular updates, and cooperation and consultation rights before any regulatory or customer notification. Address it through a specific covenant or indemnity, outside the general cap and basket.
- **Sandbar (AUD 330,000).** "Ordinary-course" is an assertion. DL para 8 says nothing on whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Request the contracts and terms, then assess. Do not agree that these are Debt or that the price should be reduced until we've done that. Equally, don't accept the Seller's characterisation.

### 5. Tax, IP and Title
- **Tax/IP.** Those terms remain open. The Seller's "settled under the general regime" claim should be rejected. Keep them as separate categories, and don't concede or assume any unlimited liability.
- **Title.** DD-012 is the Seller-supplied register, and DL para 10 itself says the Buyer hasn't completed verification. Require independent evidence: a current ASIC extract, share issue and transfer history, a confirmation that there are no encumbrances (including any Riverlark security over the shares), board and shareholder authority, and the Seller's capacity. Also include a Title warranty and a separate Title regime.

### 6. Low-priority items
- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller's disclosures don't say that consent is required. That is not confirmation that none is needed. Have the deal team review the actual clauses, including any change-of-control wording, before we decide whether either needs a CP or only a notification covenant.

## Recommendations

1. **Don't treat anything as agreed.** Confirm with Amelia Frost whether any principal-level understanding exists. Respond that all positions remain subject to Buyer mark-up.
2. **Hold the playbook numbers** (25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24 months). If we want to consider the 20% or 18-month fallbacks, ask Amelia Frost for written authority identifying this specific draft. Don't signal flexibility beforehand.
3. **Restructure the liability clauses.** Separate regimes for general warranties, Title/capacity (100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge), Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment and covenants. Delete the "limits apply to all Claims" override. Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from every limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clause.
4. **Fix disclosure and knowledge.** Specific fair disclosure only, strike 8.3, and offer a named-person, reasonable-enquiry qualifier as the only possible fallback.
5. **Tighten Completion mechanics.** Bluefen effective consent and conditions evidenced before Completion. Riverlark payout, direct repayment and releases at Completion. Bonuses as a funds-flow line item or seller-funded with on-costs.
6. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** and request payment and assignment evidence. Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.
7. **Handle the incident and Sandbar neutrally.** Preservation, investigation and update covenants for the incident, with no assumed breach or figure. Sandbar is subject to document review, with no automatic Debt or price reduction.
8. **Run independent title diligence** and send the Seller a document request list covering the Bluefen conditions, the Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment evidence, on-costs, Sandbar terms, and the lease and Mossvale clauses.

I can turn this into a mark-up issues list or a response letter to Seller's counsel if that would help.
